claims.text: A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately predict the lattice heat-transport contribution in HfNbTaTiZr.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately predict the electronic heat-transport contribution in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed potential will outperform earlier predictive approaches by at least 20% in predictive accuracy.
The relevant sample is a bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystal that may contain defects and impurities, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Chemical short-range order and defect structures are relevant components of the alloy's atomic-scale complexity.
The machine-learning potential captures complex interactions between atoms.
Capturing complex atomic interactions enables accurate, separate predictions of lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions.
The total thermal conductivity will be 12–15 W/(K m) between 300 and 1200 K.
Earlier approaches include DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates.
Earlier approaches have predictive accuracy of approximately 80%.
The proposed approach is applicable below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
The proposed approach is applicable to bulk crystals containing defects and impurities.
A deviation greater than 10% from experimental measurements is the proposed falsification threshold.
